title: 72nd National Film Awards: Kartik Aaryan, Mammootty Share Best Actor; Yami Gautam Wins Best Actress
excerpt: South Indian cinema dominates the 72nd National Film Awards as Amaran sweeps technical categories and Kalki 2898 AD wins Best Popular Film.
body:
• Kartik Aaryan and Mammootty share the Best Actor award for Chandu Champion and Bramayugam, while Yami Gautam wins Best Actress for Article 370.
  • Tamil film Amaran dominates the technical categories, winning Best Direction (Rajkumar Periasamy), Best Editing, and Best Background Score.
  • Kalki 2898 AD wins Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment; Pushpa 2 bags Best Screenplay and Best Costume Design.
  • South Indian cinema secures over a dozen awards across Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada categories, signaling the growing national footprint of regional filmmaking.

The 72nd National Film Awards were announced on Friday, recognizing the best of Indian cinema certified during the 2024 calendar year. In a ceremony that underscored the growing prominence of South Indian filmmaking, films across Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada earned more than a dozen major honours.

Kartik Aaryan and Mammootty Share Best Actor

Kartik Aaryan won his first National Award for Chandu Champion, directed by Kabir Khan, in which he portrayed the inspiring journey of Murlikant Petkar, India's first Paralympic gold medalist in swimming. He shares the honour with Malayalam veteran Mammootty, recognized for his performance in Bramayugam, a period horror film that earned critical acclaim for its atmospheric storytelling.

Yami Gautam Dhar was named Best Actress for Article 370, a political action drama directed by Aditya Suhas Jambhale. Her portrayal of an intelligence officer navigating the high-stakes mission around the abrogation of Article 370 was widely praised for its intensity and conviction.

"Article 370 was never just a film for me. It was a responsibility."

— Yami Gautam Dhar, Best Actress winner

Amaran Sweeps Technical Categories

Tamil biographical war drama Amaran, based on the life of Major Mukund Varadarajan, emerged as the most decorated film of the evening. Director Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Direction, R. Kalaivannan received Best Editing, and composer G.V. Prakash Kumar was honoured with Best Music Direction for Background Score.

Article 370 was named Best Feature Film overall. Sanjay Mishra won Best Supporting Actor for his role in the investigative drama Bhakshak, while Best Supporting Actress was shared between Ropashree Varkady (Mithya, Kannada) and Sachana Namidass (Maharaja, Tamil).

Telugu Cinema's Blockbuster Haul

Telugu cinema had a particularly strong showing. Nag Ashwin's Kalki 2898 AD won Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment and Best Production Design for Nitin Zihani Choudhary. The Pushpa sequel earned director Sukumar the Best Screenplay award, shared with Venky Atluri for Lucky Baskhar, along with Best Costume Design for Deepali Noor and Sheetal Sharma.

Niharika Konidela-backed Committee Kurrollu was named Best Telugu Film, while 35 – Chinna Katha Kaadu won Best Children's Film. Young actor Arundev Pothula from the same film received the Best Child Artist award.

Regional Cinema Shines

Tamil action-drama Captain Miller won Best Feature Film Promoting National, Social and Environmental Values, with lead actor Dhanush receiving a Special Mention for his performance. Raayan was named Best Tamil Film, while Feminichi Fathima took Best Malayalam Film. Anl Arasu won Best Action Direction for Maharaja.

Malayalam cinema added further honours with Shehnad Jalal winning Best Cinematography for Bramayugam and Vaikom Vijayalakshmi earning Best Female Playback Singer for her song in A.R.M. Kannada film Mithya earned recognition through the Best Supporting Actress and Best Child Artist (Athish S. Shetty) categories.

What It Means for Indian Cinema

The 72nd National Film Awards continue a trend that has been building for several years: South Indian cinema is no longer a regional phenomenon but a national force. Films like Kalki 2898 AD, Pushpa 2, and Amaran were among the highest-grossing Indian films of 2024, and their recognition at the National Awards validates their commercial and artistic impact.

For the Indian diaspora, several of these films are available on major streaming platforms worldwide — Amaran on Netflix, Kalki 2898 AD on Prime Video, and Bramayugam on Disney+ Hotstar — making it easier than ever to engage with the best of Indian cinema regardless of geography.

The awards ceremony, presided over by an 11-member jury led by filmmaker Jayaraj, is expected to take place in the coming weeks. The 72nd edition covers films certified by the CBFC between January 1 and December 31, 2024.
